title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
key_facts: A judge ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI's hiring materials in the trade secrets lawsuit Apple filed against OpenAI in July.

The documents cover OpenAI's interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles in its consumer hardware and robotics groups, such as interview checklists, guides, manuals, scripts and technical presentations.
The court gave OpenAI five days to hand over materials it has already collected and 14 days for the rest.
US District Judge Edward Davila also allowed Apple to see private LINE messages between individuals named in the case, including OpenAI employees Chang Liu and Alyssa Peng.
He approved depositions for Liu, Peng and OpenAI's chief hardware officer Tang Yew Tan, all former Apple employees.

He denied Apple's request to expedite access to OpenAI's research and development in areas such as metal finishes and power management, and several broader requests; the denial is not final and Apple may narrow its requests and try again.
Apple accuses OpenAI of a pattern of theft, including former employees using Apple laptops to download confidential files and coaching others on what to bring to interviews.
OpenAI is developing a consumer hardware device that could one day rival the iPhone.
